Insights & recommendations · September 2026
Insights
1
Cost efficiency
Cost per lead eased to RM15.21 this month, while cost per subscriber fell much further, to RM75.08. The difference comes down to conversion, which climbed to 20.3% from 18.1%, so a larger share of this month's leads are turning into paying subscribers, not just cheaper traffic.
2
Lead channel mix
WhatsApp Messaging remained the main driver this month, contributing 172 leads, 73% of the total. It was also this month's biggest mover, down 31, so even the dominant channel pulled back this month, worth checking whether that was intentional.
3
Conversion funnel health
20.3% of leads became subscribers this month, up 2.2 points from 18.1%, alongside a -11% increase in lead volume. Both moved in the right direction together, a good sign that the extra leads coming in are converting just as well as before.
4
Spend concentration
Prospecting | Sales Messaging | WA | In-House Content accounted for 39% of this month's spend, with a cost per lead running 4% above the account average. Since it's the largest single campaign, even a modest efficiency gain here would have an outsized effect on the account as a whole.
Recommendations
1
Budget allocation
Prospecting | Sales Messaging | WA | Agency Content produced the cheapest leads this month at RM12.68, compared to RM16.32 for Retargeting | Messaging | WA | EN CONTENT, a meaningful gap between two campaigns on the same platform. We'd recommend shifting some budget from the latter into the former next month and watching whether the cost advantage holds as spend increases.
2
Lead engagement quality
46.8% of the leads reached this month replied back the same day, up from 44.4% last month, a sign the messaging and audience are resonating well. Worth keeping the current creative and targeting approach in place as volume grows.
3
Creative refresh vs scale
DemoVideo-EN was this month's strongest performer, with 37 leads at RM12.86 each. 5 of the account's 20 active creatives are each spending under 2% of budget with little to show for it, we'd recommend shifting that spend toward the top performers and retiring or refreshing the underperforming 5.
4
Video content format
Only 47% of 3-second plays reach the 25% watched mark, the steepest drop in the funnel, and just 9% watch to the end. Since most of the loss happens right at the start, we'd recommend prioritising a stronger opening hook on new creative over changes to the middle or end of the video.
